thread:
maria: heads-up — we've seen repeated transient OOMs on prod-gpu-9a at ~12:20 UTC. 3 events in 5m, mem spike ~3.2GB above headroom during large batches. stack looks like kernel:fastpath + kvcache warmup + small workspace allocations.

deploy-bot: [alert] OOM spike on prod-gpu-9a (pod: runtime-45) — trace id=tx-9f3b. auto-sample attached.

tj: can you drop the flame link? want to check allocation timeline.

maria: flamegraph: https://internal/trace/tx-9f3b (short link). quick notes: big contiguous workspace alloc at token 128 boundary, then fragmentation when KV cache warms.

arjun: short-term mitigation: enable provisional buffer throttle for that node, reduce max_batch_size from 32 -> 16, force conservative kernel selection for sequences >512. also enable buffer-reuse path if it's off.

sarah: +1. also flip KV eviction into aggressive mode (kv_ttl=30s) so warmup doesn't create large transient working sets.

tj: what's the admin API call for the buffer throttle?

arjun: here — quick examples:
```
# runtimectl (ssh to admin host)
/runtimectl nodes throttle set --node prod-gpu-9a --policy provisional-buffer --limit 0.6

# HTTP admin API
POST /admin/nodes/prod-gpu-9a/throttle
Content-Type: application/json
{ "policy": "provisional-buffer", "limit": 0.6 }
```

maria: applying now (api). will reduce batch size and flip kernel for that node at the same time.

deploy-bot: change detected: throttle=provisional-buffer(0.6) applied by maria @ 12:27:11 UTC.

maria: throttle applied, max_batch_size=16, kernel_selector=conservative. early obs: p50 +~30ms, p95 +~120ms, no new OOMs in 4m.

tj: can we add a route-level circuit-breaker for very large requests? fail-fast above a threshold to protect the pool.

arjun: yes — config snippet:
```
route: /v1/generate
circuit_breaker: 
  request_size_threshold_tokens: 200000
  fail_mode: 503
```

sarah: I'll open a customer-facing incident note and ping on-call, product & support. ops-bot will create the incident. we should also prepare a fallback route to a smaller quantized model for the affected capacity tier.

ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-3145, pages: oncall@redwood.

arjun: for rollback criteria: if error rate > 1% or latency degradation > 2x baseline for 10m, revert throttle and kernel change. also plan to drain the node and repro locally to capture allocator histograms.

maria: summarizing the temporary playbook we executed: 1) apply provisional buffer throttle on node 2) reduce max_batch_size 3) force conservative kernel selector 4) enable aggressive kv eviction (kv_ttl=30s) 5) add route-level circuit-breaker for huge requests 6) route fallback to quantized model variant 7) monitor for 10m, revert if regression.

tj: follow-up items: add an alert for "kernel fastpath memory cliff" and instrument per-kernel workspace footprint over seq len distribution so we can auto-suggest headroom. i'll open a tiny PR.

arjun: postmortem checklist: collect allocator histograms, CUDA memory footprints per kernel, kvcache insertion rate, and per-request workspace allocations (seq len buckets 1/64/128/256/512/1024/2048).

maria: thanks everyone. no additional OOMs after changes. i'll attach the incident doc and allocator dumps to the ticket. closing thread for now, will update with postmortem link. :white_check_mark:
